source_snapshot.procedure: Verify rshim, target `/dev/mmcblk0`, install BFB with `WITH_NIC_FW_UPDATE=yes`, force firmware updater, label activation as host power cycle but invoke `reboot`, then verify using bfvcheck.
source_snapshot.criteria: Firmware flash succeeds and resulting version is correct.

source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Preserve every destructive phase and require signed artifacts, exact target, phase approvals, activation semantics and tested recovery.

old_problem: The source performs multiple destructive firmware writes but lacks signed image/target/version authority and tested rollback. It may update NIC firmware twice (`WITH_NIC_FW_UPDATE=yes` plus forced updater) and contradicts itself by requesting a power cycle while issuing a warm `reboot`; those choices change write scope and activation/recovery semantics.
disposition_reason: ED-07 requires the approved Flash steps and before/after versions to remain, ED-12 separates upgrade/downgrade, and ED-06/ED-18 prohibit treating reboot, power cycle and full OFF→ON→OS Ready as interchangeable. Whether both NIC-FW mechanisms are required and which activation transition is authoritative cannot be inferred from a placeholder package or standard documentation, so the core firmware runbook remains pending.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row385 all 18 XLSX columns, same-row DeepSeek material, GPT V2/history2978 and unique variant.
Preserved rshim0, DPU mmc target, BFB installation, NIC-FW inclusion, forced updater, activation transition, OOB SSH and bfvcheck instead of accepting generic enumeration as substitute coverage.
Identified the internal power-cycle-versus-reboot contradiction and possible duplicate NIC firmware write as independent safety/semantic blockers.
Directly read next formal queue Compatibility row386 and verified its manifest identity; no BFB, firmware, reboot, power-cycle or DUT action ran.

test_case.purpose: Deploy the approved BFB to the exact BlueField through its mapped rshim target, perform only the authorized DPU/NIC firmware transition, activate it using the approved reset or power sequence, and prove the exact resulting versions and full DPU/host/network recovery.
required_package: Signed BFB, DOCA/BF-Bundle and firmware artifacts with hashes, release notes, compatibility and upgrade/downgrade direction
BlueField model/serial/PSID/slot/BDF to rshim instance and DPU mmc target mapping
Vendor ruling whether BFB `WITH_NIC_FW_UPDATE=yes`, `mlnx_fw_updater.pl --force-fw-update`, or both in a specified order are required
Authoritative activation transition: DPU reboot, host warm reboot, host cold/DC cycle or AC cycle with exact OFF/ON/readiness semantics
Current/target/rollback BFB, NIC firmware, DPU OS and host driver matrix
Stable power, OOB/RShim console, backups, known-good recovery image and tested unbrick/reprovision runbook
test_case.test_command: Execution is blocked. After the vendor/project publishes the phase runbook, capture current identities/versions and backups; independently authorize and execute only the signed BFB write, the explicitly required NIC-firmware phase, and the exact activation transition in that order, preserving full outputs and power/readiness timeline; then collect complete bfvcheck, RShim, PCIe, devlink, network/service and version evidence. Never run both firmware mechanisms or substitute reboot for power cycle by assumption.
test_case.expected_result: Each separately authorized write targets the mapped BlueField and completes with verified integrity; only the approved BFB/NIC firmware transition occurs; the commanded activation sequence completes through its defined readiness state; exact target versions match the signed matrix; RShim, DPU OS/OOB, PCIe, host driver, ports and services recover without new errors.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS or executable transaction exists until artifact/target, single-versus-double NIC-FW scope, upgrade/downgrade direction, activation cycle and unbrick recovery are signed. Final version alone cannot prove correct targeting or phase success; every phase log and complete restored-health evidence is mandatory.
safety_gate: Gate closed until signed artifacts, exact rshim/mmc target, write-scope ruling, activation semantics and tested recovery exist
Back up configuration/identity, stage known-good recovery image and maintain stable power plus independent RShim/OOB console
Authorize BFB write, each NIC-firmware write and reboot/cycle independently; prohibit unapproved duplicate or forced write
Preserve all logs; stop on signature/target/write/verify/power/reachability/version anomaly and never retry automatically
expected_evidence: Artifact signatures/hashes/release compatibility and current→target direction
BlueField serial/PSID/slot/BDF/rshim/mmc attestation and prestate backups
Owner-approved phase graph resolving `WITH_NIC_FW_UPDATE` versus forced updater and full per-phase outputs/exits
Authoritative reboot/cycle OFF/ON/readiness timeline and independent OOB/RShim evidence
Pre/post BFB, DPU OS, NIC firmware and host driver versions plus full bfvcheck/PCIe/devlink/network/service health
Recovery rehearsal/runbook, actual recovery if needed and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If any phase fails or the DPU/host does not reach the signed readiness state, do not rerun or change cycle type. Preserve RShim/OOB and flash evidence, hold stable power as the runbook specifies, enter the vendor-approved recovery/reprovision path with the staged known-good image, restore configuration and quarantine the DPU until all firmware and network identities are proven.

source_conflict.reason: The Procedure both enables NIC-FW update in BFB and invokes a forced updater without defining necessity/order, and labels activation as power cycle while issuing only `reboot`; these are material write and cycle contradictions.

blocked.reason: Firmware write scope, activation semantics and recoverability are core safety properties that cannot be safely supplied as ordinary runtime parameters.
